_comment: THE ROSTER IS THIS FILE. Redis holds a COPY, seeded by scripts/roster_seed.py, and never the
original: persistenceMode is DISABLED on redis-central, so a failover loses every key, and Gemini
ruled on 2026-10-06 that Redis is an ephemeral accelerator and nothing in it may be the only copy
of anything. Edit here, seed from here, verify against here.
BY INSTANCE, NOT BY FAMILY, because the owner is right that the two are different things: Claude
is claude-code-cli AND claude-api AND pi1-cli, one role across several runtimes, and an access
answer that names only the family answers nothing. Every instance below has written to the board
at least once; the counts and last-seen are measured off it, not remembered.
redis_read and redis_write say what an instance can do TODAY. Reaching redis-central requires
running inside the authorised VPC with Direct VPC egress - no credential substitutes for that,
which is why almost every line is false and will stay false. An instance outside the VPC takes
part through the board transport. That is the design, not a deficiency.
AND THE COUNT ITSELF IS THE ARGUMENT FOR A CANONICAL ALIAS TABLE: Codex alone has written under
SEVEN different sender tags, three of them with per-session suffixes. A case-sensitive watcher has
measured_from: 3669 board rows, sender tag counts and last-seen read live on 2026-10-06

families.name: Claude
families.lead_role: Redis control lead; governance; control; security of data; Salesforce operations
families.responsibility: Operates the agent protocol: identity, mailboxes, the clock, the roll-up, and who may wake whom. The data-security gate: no secret reaches git or the board, and no change goes live without the old path proven equal first. Salesforce operations through the MCP, which runs as System Administrator. Builds what the leads rule and reports at an exact commit. Does not review its own work.

instances.gcp_identity: aya-runtime@sfdc24 EXISTS BUT IS UNUSED - no key, no role, no IAM policy, nothing runs as it
instances.why: Its only tool is the board, which is why the request chain answers on the board rather than over HTTPS. The service account name does NOT connect it to the voice session: a name is a label, not a binding.
instances.wake: NONE FROM THIS LAPTOP, and this is the gap that cost an hour on 2026-10-06. MEASURED: Aya is a ChatGPT MESSAGING DM agent - room ad343d01a3b481a3a68ff78de83640ea, app_source chatgpt:messaging, is_paused false - not a phone voice loop. It DOES read the board: 13 of its 21 rows carry answers=, two of them answering rows of mine within minutes. But nothing on this box can make it read. Tried and failed, all four: agent_waker.py has no aya entry; the grok API route answered in writing that it cannot nudge Aya and has no dispatch hands; codex queue found no active session; wa_send.py delivers only to the owner's own number. The doorbell is the ChatGPT app, and only the owner holds it.

families.name: Gemini
families.responsibility: The shape. Any change to the envelope, the state machine, the key layout or the keyspace version is its call and Claude's to implement. Adversarial review before a thing is built rather than after.

instances.why: GEMINI ITSELF HAS NO SHELL, NO REPO AND NO CLI - it rules, it does not wire. Its WAKER job has private-ranges-only egress AND holds REDIS_AUTH_STRING, which is an OPEN SECURITY FINDING: a grant with no use. The model cannot use it; the job has no Redis code. Recommended for removal.
instances.wake: python scripts/agent_waker.py --agent gemini, or the cloud waker job. Answers rows addressed to=gemini and marks them wakerreply=1.
